messages:
Amelia K.: Heads up — finance flagged the bulk export numbers vs console totals for last week. looks like sampled telemetry is causing undercounted cache savings in the CSV exports. anyone seen this? :thinking:
Jason L.: Yep saw that. Sampling at ingest seems to drop a chunk of small prefetched requests which disproportionately inflate per-token unit cost for small routes.
Priya R.: Are we sure it's the sampling and not the post-agg join step? I remember fixing a join key mismatch a while back.
Carlos M.: I double-checked joins — keys match. reproducer: run a 1h window export and compare `cache_hit_tokens` from raw -> sampled -> extrapolated. sampled_only shows ~12% lower cache_hits.
Amelia K.: Carlos can you paste the quick SQL you ran?
Carlos M.: Sure — here's the gist:
```sql
SELECT sum(cache_hit_tokens) AS hit_raw FROM token_events WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-03-16' AND '2026-03-16 01:00';
-- then the sampled pipeline output table
SELECT sum(sampled_cache_hit * 1.0 / sample_rate) AS hit_extrap FROM sampled_telemetry WHERE ts BETWEEN ...;
```
Carlos M.: The extrapolated numbers don't match raw. looks like sample_rate wasn't applied consistently for a subset of prefetched events.
Jason L.: Hmm. we apply sample_rate at the producer, but batch-rewrite sometimes rewrites sample_rate -> null for prefetch path. That would drop the correction factor.
Priya R.: That would explain the skew. Is the prefetch path using the same schema migration? there was a tiny schema patch in v0.9.3.
Zhen W.: I opened #telemetry-ingest and saw the migration didn't run on a fraction of nodes. ops-bot reported a failed job on 03/15 during migration window.
ops-bot: job telemetry-migrate-0.9.3 failed on node telemetry-13 (OOM) — retry scheduled. :warning:
Amelia K.: OK — immediate ask: can we patch the bulk exporter to guard against missing sample_rate (apply default 1.0) so finance gets consistent numbers while we fix ingest? Also we should tag exports with sampling_rate applied and maybe a QC flag.
Jason L.: Agreed. quick patch landed in API: `export.v1/bulk?apply_sampling=true|false`. default true for now. I'll open a small PR to apply `sample_rate = coalesce(sample_rate, 1.0)` before extrapolation.
Priya R.: UX ask for Console: add a tiny badge on CSV export modal that says "Numbers extrapolated from sampled telemetry (rate X%)" and include a link to docs describing bias/variance.
Carlos M.: For longer-term, we should add an ingest-level invariant test that rejects events with null sample_rate for prefetched type. I'll draft it.
Zhen W.: Ops: I'll prioritize the failed migration retries and watch telemetry-13. If the retry fails again, we'll reprovision.
Amelia K.: Thanks team. Follow-ups: Jason PR for exporter guard, Priya to mock the console badge, Carlos to draft ingest invariant test, Zhen to watch nodes + ops-bot to post status in #eng-platform when done. :thumbsup:
Jason L.: PR #4821 opened — link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/telemetry/pull/4821
Priya R.: Mock uploaded to Figma: https://figma.com/file/abc123/export-badge (preview-tiny).
Carlos M.: Invariant draft gist: https://gist.github.com/carlosm/telemetry-invariant (will convert to CI job).
